description: Aircraft Commander is pilot in command of the tasked C-17 sortie.
Loadmaster rigs and releases Container Delivery System (CDS) bundles via the airdrop release mechanism.
Aircraft Commander communicates with Air Traffic Control and ground drop-zone personnel via the tactical communications system.

description: Loadmaster coordinates drop timing and drop-zone readiness with the Drop Zone Support Team Leader before releasing CDS bundles. This is a doctrinal/structural relationship, not a direct radio link — physically, the DZSTL's radio contact is with the flight deck (see dzstl-informs-aircraft-commander-of-dz-status), relayed to the Loadmaster via aircraft intercom (see aircraft-commander-informs-loadmaster-of-release-command).

description: Drop Zone Support Team Leader relays surface wind and limited weather observations to the flight deck (Aircraft Commander) via the dz-safety-of-flight-radio-net — the actual first hop of the information path that ultimately reaches the Loadmaster relayed through the flight deck. This radio contact is limited to safety-of-flight matters (ATC directions, range clearance, unsafe surface conditions, mission changes) and wind/weather, not continuous chatter, and is mandatory (not just customary) for IMC/AWADS instrument drops.

doctrineSource.note: Enriched 2026-09-07 with the specific limited-traffic/IMC-AWADS-mandatory detail — same verification status as the dz-safety-of-flight-radio-net System record's citation.

description: Aircraft Commander relays drop-zone status/wind updates during the run-in and gives the verbal release command ("Mark") to the Loadmaster via intercom — the trigger for the Loadmaster's release-execution decision.

doctrineSource.publication: C-17 Pilot (c17pilot.com), "C-17 Airdrop Operations — How Cargo and Troops Exit at 25,000 Feet"

description: Loadmaster confirms release completion ("Cargo away") to the flight deck via intercom immediately after executing the release.
